A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BFM-SWM and BFM-VM research. The main text, algorithms, equations, three figures, and Appendices A–D are readable and can be matched across versions despite reflow.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendices C–D report original experiments on influence maximization and CIFAR-10 crowdsourcing, including objective values, oracle-query counts, and running times.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments on both applications and reports revised efficiency measurements for influence maximization.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1 and 2 introduce persistent seller ownership. Previously, reconsidered sellers could select a candidate sequence by maximum marginal gain each round; v2 routes previously inserted sellers to their permanent owner sequence. This changes candidate construction and potentially subsequent prices, enforcing disjoint aggregate sequences.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate influence maximization on Slashdot, Email, and Epinions, and valuation maximization using the same three CIFAR-10 categories. The new discussion of Nash welfare and XOS/subadditive valuations concerns future work only.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain Deng-Distorted, Deng-ROI, and Deng-CostScaled for influence maximization, and TripleEagleNm and SIP for crowdsourcing. No comparator is added or removed from either comparison.

E3.justification: The stated budget sweeps, metrics, baseline prefix-truncation procedure, theory-derived parameters, error parameter of 0.1, and CIFAR-10 construction remain unchanged. The revised efficiency plots are not accompanied by a reported evaluation-protocol change.

E4.justification: The same budget-dependent comparisons and supplementary runtime comparisons are retained. Neither version adds component ablations, robustness tests, error analyses, or new sensitivity questions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical tests. The updated plotted measurements do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Efficiency results are substantially revised across the three network datasets: Figure 1(d–f) lowers Deng-ROI and Deng-CostScaled query counts, and Figure 3 replaces runtime curves and changes some baseline rankings. For example, Deng-CostScaled becomes faster than Deng-Distorted on Slashdot, reversing v1. Objective-value curves and the reported 4.49-fold average welfare advantage remain unchanged; Figure 2 and its 21.85% and 5.27% gains are also retained.

T1.justification: Definition 4.2 replaces overlapping exclusion categories with first-insertion classes, rejection before insertion, and a residual singleton class. The candidate-state definition is corrected, and Appendices A.2 and A.6 revise the charging arguments and explicitly use disjoint aggregate sequences. These are substantive repairs to the approximation proofs, although theorem statements and approximation constants remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Section 1.1 narrows BFM-VM's claim from preserving all economic properties to preserving budget feasibility, truthfulness, and individual rationality. This aligns the introduction with Section 5's already-existing exception for non-negative auctioneer surplus. The principal novelty, approximation, and runtime claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The conclusion replaces generic future-work wording with specific directions involving Nash welfare and XOS/subadditive valuations, and acknowledges that extending the analysis beyond submodularity requires new techniques. It also identifies lower bounds as an open problem. Existing empirical interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The source-code footnote replaces an anonymous 4open.science repository with a named GitHub repository. Hardware, parameter disclosures, and data-processing information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning against prior research are retained. Changes to the Bichler, Jalaly–Tardos, and Singer entries concern bibliographic metadata rather than different works or revised research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 locally expands the ownership explanation and proof prose, revises the conclusion, adds acknowledgments and correspondence information, and corrects the template running header. The overall section organization and most introductory, related-work, and experimental prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 3 are redrawn with revised axis ranges or labels, and Figure 1 gains a logarithmic-scale caption. Algorithm boxes expand, and appendix floats move, including Figure 2 appearing before its explanatory text. The same three figures and overall document format are retained.

improvement.justification: The ownership rule and revised definitions and proofs repair a central missing disjointness invariant and associated charging arguments supporting the non-monotone approximation guarantees. This substantially strengthens the paper's main theoretical contribution. The introductory guarantee is also made consistent with Section 5. The efficiency revisions remain unexplained, and Figure 1's new logarithmic-scale caption overgeneralizes beyond its query panels, but these limitations do not outweigh the theoretical repair.
